title: Review of c02's FCH chemoton: bodies form from noise and persist (S, I), but the claimed K-coated vesicle forms in 1 of 5 fresh runs, K-free bodies persist just as well on bath-shared amphiphile, and a feed cut shrinks bodies without killing any by t=600; at dt/2, 2 of 3 seeds lose the catalyst entirely
summary: Fresh seeds 5 (labkit, fed and feed-cut) and 6 (exact branched fork with per-body fates), plus the world at half its own step on seeds 0, 2 and 5. Bilayer worms, rings and vesicles form from noise on every run. The claimed individual, a vesicle with K on its bilayer, appears only on dt/2 seed 0 (K rim/core 4.0). On seeds 5 and 6 the catalyst sits on one open rod, and K-free bodies, including a multilamellar vesicle, keep their size on amphiphile shared through the bath. Cutting the feed at a fork shrinks every body (vesicle 2133 -> 462 px) but loses none by t=600. At dt/2, K goes extinct on seeds 2 and 5 and almost all amphiphile decays, so whether the catalyst establishes is fragile to the integration step.

seeds_run.result: fail for B/E: K only on an open rod, K-free bodies persist; feed cut shrinks all 7, none lost
fail for B/E: K only on a rod; K-free multilamellar vesicle persists fed; starved bodies shrink, none lost by t=600
pass for the K layer at dt/2 (K-coated vesicle track #13, K rim/core 4.0)

controls_run.E: rerun_starve/ (seed 5, feed cut at 300 vs rerun/) and fork_s6/ (exact branched fork): bodies shrink, none die by t=600

verdicts.limitation: B: the K layer is real where it forms (K self-made by autocatalysis and held by the bilayer mobility gate) but it formed on a vesicle in only 1 of my 5 runs; on the others K is on an open rod or extinct, so the claimed individual is not a typical outcome. E: amphiphile made only by K and decaying everywhere is E by construction; the dependence is shared, not individual: K-free bodies on seeds 5 and 6 persist at constant size on the K-bearer's product, and the fork shows shrinkage, not deaths, within 300 t (RUBRIC L4c asks for individuals that die). dt/2 changes the outcome qualitatively on 2 of 3 seeds (K extinct), which I cannot separate from per-seed chance without more seeds at both steps.
